work.what: hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_QUARTIC_HEIGHT.md answers, without a live literature-search tool, the question of whether an unconditional theorem bounds the height-integrated, q-and-character-averaged fourth moment J(X,Y) = sum_{q<=X} sum_{chi mod q}^* integral_{|t|<=Y} |L(1/2+it,chi)|^4 dt with a genuine power saving over the trivial (Cauchy-Schwarz via the second moment) bound, uniformly in both X and Y. Its answer, drawn from the model's own trained knowledge rather than a verified search, is no: it names three nearby but distinct unconditional results -- (a) Heath-Brown (Analysis 1 (1981), 25-32), Soundararajan (Clay Math Proc. 7, 2007), and Young (Annals of Math 173 (2011), 1-50), all q-and-chi-averaged fourth moments AT A FIXED POINT t=0, none integrated over t; (b) Ingham (1926), Heath-Brown (Proc. LMS (3) 38 (1979), 385-422), and Motohashi's spectral explicit formula (Acta Math. 170 (1993), 181-220, and Spectral Theory of the Riemann Zeta-Function, Cambridge Tracts 127, 1997) with refinements by Ivic, all t-integrated fourth moments for a SINGLE FIXED character (or zeta), none averaged over q; (c) the classical joint large sieve for Dirichlet L-functions (Montgomery and Vaughan, Multiplicative Number Theory I, Ch. 7; Iwaniec and Kowalski, Analytic Number Theory, Theorem 7.34 region), which is jointly (q,chi,t)-averaged but is only a SECOND moment, so combining it with the unconditional convexity bound via Cauchy-Schwarz reproduces exactly the trivial bound the question excludes as a baseline, not an improvement on it -- and argues, aspect by aspect, that none of (a), (b), (c) can be composed into a genuine joint fourth-moment bound, because each is proved by a method built to exploit cancellation in exactly one aspect. Task: with a live literature-search tool (arXiv, MathSciNet, zbMATH, or general web search), check this negative finding directly. Specifically look for: (1) any paper proving an asymptotic or power-saving upper bound for J(X,Y) itself, jointly uniform in X and Y, by any method (spectral, shifted-convolution, moment-recipe/CFKRS-conditional-on-nothing, or otherwise); (2) any extension of Young's 2011 fourth-moment-of-Dirichlet-L-functions result, or of Motohashi's spectral fourth-moment formula for zeta/Dirichlet L-functions, to a setting where BOTH the modulus/character aspect and the height aspect are allowed to grow simultaneously; (3) whether recent (post-2011) work by authors such as Blomer, Fouvry, Kowalski, Michel, Milicevic, Nunes, Petrow, or Young on moments of families of L-functions has produced anything of this joint shape, even conditionally or in a restricted range. Report back precisely: does such a theorem exist (with full citation), and if so what power-saving exponent does it prove and over what ranges of X and Y is it valid uniformly; if not, confirm the negative finding stands. Do not attempt the separate arc-transfer question (RANK3_ROUTE_D.md Section 7 already shows no transfer exists for Z_(q) by the method that works for U_(q); RANK3_QUARTIC_HEIGHT.md Section 4 already confirms the L-function-moment literature does not supply an alternative transfer route either) -- this task is a literature-verification task only, not a new derivation.
